questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to go on exchange due to personal growth in a new envoirement, which was my main reason for choosing to attend UCD. Academic and career opporitunities were also part of the reason, since I tried being more on my own feet in a academic envoirement, which I have learned so much in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Even though I arrived after orientations, due to exams at my home university, the journey of going on exchange with all the people and academics could not have been more perfect.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not quite since I missed orientation, but UCD were very accomendating with any questions I had, which helped.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a contact person, a cara, which whoom I met up with and got an introduction to the university and he answeared all my questions. Otherwise non were given.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were some webinairs before arrival, which were very helpful as well with what we needed to do before arriving on campus etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were different types of appartments on campus, which worked out great. The only downside was that the price for acommondation were very high, especially for what you got for the money.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The kitchen was the biggest downfall for the appartment. For the sum of over €1100 a month I would expect at least an oven, which wasn't in the appartment. There was provided a stove, microwave, kettle (which wasn't clean) and a toaster. Another thing that took the experience down was that the kitchen was completely empty with no plates, cups, pots or pans. We all needed to buy new stuff and at the end of our stay there was a donation event on campus, but it got full. Therefore we had to throw a bunch of good stuff out, which is super wastefull.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That eventhough it is expensive you meet so many amazing people and events on campus and it makes it a lot easier to get around campus to class and meet up with all your new friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to pick a top 3 housing types, where after it was dealt out amongst the students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a webinair, which was very helpful and you could look on the residence portal for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got my first priority.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That it is a university that you can always seek help from, with their 24 hour reception being open.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I too two leve 3 and one level 4, so level 4 would be like a masters course for me at my home university, but not at the host institution since they have a 4 year bachelor.
I picked some out of interests and others I choose due to them not having an exam to ensure that I had more time to be in the lab and work on my bachelor thesis.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found it very different in terms of the materials provided for the courses. At UCPH we have books and reading materials before each lectrure, so that the students are prepared for the lectures. Thereby the lectures are secondary learning and books primary. At the host institution there were nu reading material for the lectures and only things for "additional reading". The slides were therefore primary learning and books or articles were secondary.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PHAR30110-Cardiovascular & Renal Disease-2023/24 Spring
BMOL30100-Lead Teams in Sci Enterprise-2023/24 Spring
BIOC40220-Hot topics in Biochemistry-2023/24 Spring
BMOL40330-Biomol. Sci. Research Project-2023/24 Spring

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Hot Topics in Biochemestry for sure! It was a nice course, where you were introduced to reading and presenting scientific materials, which you might not be fully comfortable in. This was a really fun and cool experience for review and get exposed to so many different types and corners of science.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It depends on how many trips you go on additionally. There is a lot to see and experience in the country, so you also have to put that under your personal spendings. Ryanair is tho so cheap, which is nice.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It were more expensive than expected, especially due to the high rent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot of sports opporitunities, which you can join for a small fee. I joined handball and it helped me make some good friends in the end.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plenty of societies, sports clubs and trips planned to different places in the country.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sports team, it is a great place to meet a lot of good people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips to the countryside or neighboring cities. It is a lovely country in Ireland and loads of places to take amazing hikes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy coming from another northern european nation.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just try and come to as much as possible even though it is scary in the beginning, cause everyone is in the same boat and want to make friends. This is the way I met some of my best friends there, which is friends for life after sharing this experience together.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is a difference in food which I had to get used to. The drinking culture on clubs and pubs were also very different. Both for good and for worse. Clothing were also very different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved how friendly and open the Irish people were. I also loved that the pubs were open all day and you would find people in Dublin enjoying each others company. My favorite were Sct. Patricks day I would have to say :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Amazing social life, Loads of travel opporitunities and loads of craigh (fun in Irish)!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Comparing to some of my fellow student on other universities it was clear that we got a lot of support before arrival to the university. Here we could choose bachelor project and courses before hand, which wasn't the case for all destinations. Therefore it was a more calming journey leading up to the big change in moving there.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people I met on my stay. When staying on campus and having roomates, who are from all over the world, it got very easy to meet more and more people. That made my whole stay worth so much.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think it was meeting people when arriving after orientation. But it took a couple weeks and I ended up being so comfortable with my friends, so it all worked out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
